_meta.indication: ATTRUBY is a transthyretin stabilizer indicated for the treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or variant transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular death and cardiovascular-related hospitalization.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-arm parallel trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to acoramidis 712 mg (800 mg acoramidis HCl) twice daily or matching placebo, followed for 30 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with symptomatic wild-type or variant transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: a hierarchical combination of all-cause mortality (ACM), cumulative frequency of CV-related hospitalizations (CVH), change from baseline in NT-proBNP, and change from baseline in 6MWD over the 30-month trial duration.
pivotal_trials.n: 632 randomized (421 acoramidis, 211 placebo); mITT efficacy population N=611.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint met: Win ratio 1.77 (96% CI 1.40, 2.24), p<0.0001; at 30 months 81% alive on acoramidis versus 74% on placebo and fewer CVH events (0.3 versus 0.6 per year).

key_safety: Higher frequency of gastrointestinal adverse reactions with ATTRUBY: diarrhea 11.6% vs 7.6% and upper abdominal pain 5.5% vs 1.4% versus placebo; most were mild. Discontinuation due to an adverse event was similar (9.3% vs 8.5%).
target_moa: Acoramidis is a selective stabilizer of transthyretin (TTR); it binds TTR at thyroxine binding sites and slows dissociation of the TTR tetramer into its constituent monomers, the rate-limiting step in amyloidogenesis.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held; the application did not raise significant or controversial issues warranting outside expertise.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted October 2, 2018 (DRU-2017-5931) for the treatment of transthyretin amyloidosis.

citations.quote: Acoramidis received orphan drug designation (DRU-2017-5931) on October 2, 2018, for the treatment of transthyretin amyloidosis and is therefore exempt from Pediatric Research Equity Act requirements.

summary.text: NDA 216540 was a standard (non-priority) review for the new molecular entity acoramidis, with orphan drug designation for transthyretin amyloidosis; approval was based on the single phase 3 trial AG10-301 (ATTRibute-CM) and no Advisory Committee was convened.

citations.quote:
Priority or standard	STANDARD
Submit date(s)	11/29/2023
Acoramidis received orphan drug designation on October 2, 2018, for the treatment of transthyretin amyloidosis.
This NDA is based on the single, adequate, and well-controlled trial AG10-301 (ATTRibute-CM Trial).
The application did not raise significant or controversial issues that would warrant outside expertise or public discussion; as such, no Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application.

requirement.text: 4726-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to acoramidis during pregnancy or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
